paper_title: DraftAttention: Fast Video Diffusion via Low-Resolution Attention Guidance
original_abstract: Diffusion transformer–based video generation models (DiTs) have recently attracted widespread attention for their excellent generation quality. However, their computational cost remains a major bottleneck—attention alone accounts for over 80% of total latency, and generating just 8 seconds of 720p video takes tens of minutes—posing serious challenges to practical application and scalability. To address this, we propose the DraftAttention, a training-free framework for the acceleration of video diffusion transformers with dynamic sparse attention on GPUs. We apply down-sampling to each feature map across frames in the compressed latent space, enabling a higher-level receptive field over the latent composed of hundreds of thousands of tokens. The low-resolution draft attention map, derived from draft query and key, exposes redundancy both spatially within each feature map and temporally across frames. We reorder the query, key, and value based on the draft attention map to guide the sparse attention computation in full resolution, and subsequently restore their original order after the attention computation. This reordering enables structured sparsity that aligns with hardware-optimized execution. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that the low-resolution draft attention closely approximates the full attention, providing reliable guidance for constructing accurate sparse attention. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing sparse attention approaches in video generation quality and achieves up to 1.75× end-to-end speedup on GPUs.

innovations.name: Low-Resolution Draft Attention
innovations.description: Uses average pooling to create downsampled query and key representations for efficient attention computation
innovations.runtime_change: [n, n, d] → [n/128, n/128, d] for draft computation
innovations.benefit: Reduces quadratic complexity by 128× for draft attention

innovations.name: Dynamic Sparse Patterns
innovations.description: Generates prompt-dependent sparse attention patterns for each attention module dynamically
innovations.runtime_change: Static [n, n, d] → Dynamic r-sparse [n, n, d] where r ∈ {0.55, 0.75, 0.9}

innovations.name: Hardware-Friendly Reordering
innovations.description: Deterministic token reordering to ensure contiguous memory access for sparse computation
innovations.runtime_change: Adds O(n) reordering overhead before/after attention

innovations.name: Training-Free Integration
innovations.description: Plug-and-play module requiring no additional training or fine-tuning
innovations.runtime_change: No training time, direct inference application

gaps_and_limitations.description: Uses static 8×16 pooling kernel regardless of video resolution or content
gaps_and_limitations.impact: Suboptimal for non-divisible resolutions or varying content complexity

gaps_and_limitations.description: Same sparsity ratio applied across all attention layers and timesteps
gaps_and_limitations.impact: May over-sparsify important layers or under-sparsify redundant ones

gaps_and_limitations.description: Average pooling treats temporal and spatial dimensions equally
gaps_and_limitations.impact: Misses temporal attention patterns that could guide better sparsity

gaps_and_limitations.description: No distributed computing or multi-GPU support
gaps_and_limitations.impact: Limited scalability for longer videos or higher resolutions

gaps_and_limitations.description: Uses full precision despite mentioning quantization as future work

proposed_improvements.description: Dynamic kernel size selection based on resolution and content complexity
proposed_improvements.implementation: Use multi-scale pooling with learnable kernel selection per layer
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [n, n, d] → [n/k_i, n/k_i, d] where k_i ∈ {64, 128, 256} adaptive

proposed_improvements.description: Dynamic sparsity ratios based on attention entropy and layer depth
proposed_improvements.implementation: Compute attention entropy per layer to guide sparsity ratio r_i ∈ [0.5, 0.95]
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: Adds O(g²) entropy computation per layer

proposed_improvements.description: Separate temporal and spatial pooling with motion-aware sparsity
proposed_improvements.implementation: 3D pooling (T×H×W) with motion vector analysis for temporal sparsity
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [n_t×n_s, n_t×n_s, d] → [n_t/k_t, n_s/k_s, d] with k_t ≠ k_s

proposed_improvements.description: Parallel draft computation across GPUs with gradient sparsity
proposed_improvements.implementation: Ring-allreduce for draft attention + pipeline parallel sparse attention
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [n, n, d] → ([n/p, n, d] + [n, n/p, d]) with p GPUs + communication
proposed_improvements.communication_time: O(g²d/p) for draft sync + O(rn²d/p) for sparse gather
proposed_improvements.expected_speedup: Linear scaling with GPUs (up to 8× with 8 GPUs)

proposed_improvements.description: 8-bit quantization for draft computation with mixed-precision sparse attention
proposed_improvements.implementation: INT8 for draft Q/K/V + FP16 for critical sparse attention blocks
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [n/128, n/128, d] INT8 + [n, n, d] mixed-precision

proposed_improvements.description: Trainable draft tokens that adapt to specific video domains
proposed_improvements.implementation: Lightweight MLP to learn optimal draft representations per domain
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: Adds O(kd) parameters where k ≪ n (negligible)

improved_method.multi_gpu: [n/p, n, d] + [n, n/p, d] with p GPUs

improved_runtime_breakdown.temporal_guidance: [n_t/k_t, n_s/k_s, d] with motion-aware k_t, k_s
improved_runtime_breakdown.multi_gpu_comm: [n/p, n, d] + [n, n/p, d] + O(g²d/p) comm
